Their published figures showed that the share of women among STEM graduates was higher in more gender-equal countries, a pattern that cannot be squared with the paradox they named, since the two characterizations of the same correlation cannot both be true. Correlational cross-national work is only as strong as the construction of its propensity measures, and its evidential weight collapses when the computation cannot be recovered from the published description. Interest inventories establish robust average differences in what people say they want, but they cannot by themselves distinguish preferences formed under constraint from preferences formed freely.
